summary: v2 of the plan-phase risk register — replan iteration 1 (HITL kickback). The operator's directive declared the cache-TTL question EMPIRICALLY CLOSED (both Anthropic and Qwen routes hand-measured to survive >=60-min idle with zero cache re-creation; no keep-warm needed on either route) and ordered slice-1 to stop re-deriving it. Surgical update to v1: (a) the Qwen-route cache-TTL ceiling is moved from `risks` to `operator_settled_inputs` — it is no longer a risk to mitigate; (b) BC-1 (egg-harness cache instrumentation gap) is REFRAMED — the live risk is whether the egg-prefix per-event prompt assembly actually HITS the cached prefix on each event (cache-breakpoint placement + cache_read ratio), NOT whether the cache survives long enough; (c) R-11 (slice-8 conditional keep-warm stall) is obsolete — architect's v4 slice DAG re-purposes slice-8 to prompt collapse (cq-1 MCP-split deferred), so the keep-warm conditional no longer exists in any slice; (d) R-14 (litellm-log scrape fragility) narrows to cost-instrumentation side effect (cache_read/cache_creation tokens) — no longer a dedicated TTL-bracketing spike; (e) new R-17 flags the recurrence risk that task_planner v4's slice-1 re-author might leave latent TTL-bracketing language in task-1-3 AC / task-1-4 report question, contradicting the operator directive. Everything else in the register is unchanged — the 8/9 of the plan the operator endorsed (slice-8 collapse, cq-1 MCP-split, cq-3 durable budget, cq-4 full deletion of capped-restart wrapper, brc-memory.md ephemeral, python3 -m egg_agent harness primitive, real egg_stack integration fixture) remains correctly risk-assessed. Verdict on the plan as scaffolded remains ACK conditional on the surgical TTL strip landing in task_planner v4. If task_planner v4 re-introduces TTL bracketing language in slice-1, this verdict converts to NACK with R-17 / BC-1-v2 as the blocking citation.
verdict_rationale: ACK applies to the plan as currently scaffolded in contract.slices[0..8] PROVIDED task_planner v4 strips the TTL-bracketing language per the operator directive: (1) task-1-3 AC must remove 'at least 3 idle durations (5.5, 10, 15 min)' and the litellm-log-derived TTL-survival framing; (2) task-1-3 description must remove 'Repeat for 5.5 min and 10 min idles to bracket the TTL ceiling'; (3) task-1-4 report question (b) — 'what Qwen-route TTL ceiling did the measurements show — survives >= 15 min, lapses 5.5-15 min, or ambiguous?' — must be removed. What survives in slice-1 per the directive: (a) per-event cost / wall-clock instrumentation through python3 -m egg_agent with the production BRC preamble + tool schemas (BC-1 reframed, instrument-only, no fail thresholds — feedback-1 Q1); (b) event-pump-reaches-consensus de-risk on the #2906 repro (task-1-2 unchanged). Cache_read/cache_creation token counts may be recorded as a SIDE EFFECT of cost measurement (legitimate per directive), but the dedicated idle-duration TTL-ceiling spike and any stop/go gate keyed on TTL are forbidden. Re-evaluation hook: when architect v5 (if respin) and task_planner v4 PROPOSE, this verdict is re-applied to their concrete proposals; R-17 / BC-1-v2 / rubric items in review_targets convert to NACK if unaddressed in the final proposal.

risks.title: Egg-prefix cache-breakpoint placement may bust prefix cache on every event (REFRAMED — TTL ceiling concern moved to OSI-1)
risks.description: The cache-survival TTL question is settled (OSI-1). The remaining live risk is whether the egg-prefix per-event prompt assembly actually HITS the cached prefix on each event, vs. busting it because dynamic content (memory snapshot, NACK reasons, version delta, pipeline-id, role, slice-id) lands BEFORE the cache breakpoint. The egg prefix is materially larger and structurally different from the raw-claude prefix that operator-measured cache-survival on: it includes the BRC preamble assembled at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py::_build_brc_preamble:12348, mission.md (sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md ~195 lines), and 28 MCP tool schemas registered via sandbox/egg_agent_tools/tools/*. If the new wrapper template (slice-5) places per-event dynamic content before the cache breakpoint, every event busts the prefix on BOTH routes regardless of TTL — and the central economic argument for event-pump (bounded per-event cost via cache_read) collapses. The risk is structural prompt assembly, NOT cache survival.
evidence_files: sandbox/egg_agent_tools/tools/* (28 MCP tool schemas, per WS8)
Operator iteration-1 directive (TTL closed); cache_read RATIO on egg-prefix structure remains unmeasured
risks.mitigation: Slice-1 task-1-2 (event-pump prototype run) MUST capture per-event prompt_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens from python3 -m egg_agent invocations with the production BRC preamble + tool schemas. This is the BC-1-v2 instrumentation — instrument-only, no threshold gate (OSI-2). Slice-5 (event-pump wrapper template) must define and assert breakpoint placement in a unit test: dynamic content (memory-file path, event-json) goes in the SUFFIX (post-breakpoint), with the BRC preamble + tool schemas frozen as PREFIX. Slice-8 prompt collapse (per architect v4 slice-8) is the place to lock breakpoint discipline into the prompt-assembly path.

risks.title: Trust-boundary drift on cost instrumentation path
risks.description: Per #2594, runtime-primitive and trust-boundary mismatches are a recurring high-impact failure mode. Concrete instance: the issue body WS7 comment references `~/.local/state/clm/cost-*.json` as the cost-callback source on the Qwen route. Empirical check: grep across the repo for `cost-.*\.json` and `\.local/state/clm` returns hits ONLY in .egg-state/brc-history/ (prior pipeline logs), NOT as a live artifact in this repo. The production path is config/litellm/cost_callback.py which logs to stdout only (lines 238-241) and holds in-memory LRU per session (lines 75-76). The contract has corrected this in task-1-3 ('source Qwen cache-read counts from the litellm container's structured logs via `kubectl logs deployment/egg-litellm`'), but the correction is only as good as the test infrastructure that exercises it. Tests run outside k3s won't have `kubectl logs` available, and a stubbed equivalent must be wired.
risks.mitigation: task-1-3 corrects the source path. After the operator's TTL strip (iteration-1 directive), the litellm-log adapter is still needed — but now ONLY for the cost-instrumentation side effect (per-event prompt_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_tokens on the Qwen route, where Claude Code's `usage.*` returns all-zero per refine analysis). Slice-9 integration validation must run with the same adapter, not a separate k3s-only path that diverges. NOTE: the prior 'reused by slice-8 TASK-8-1' rationale is OBSOLETE — slice-8 is now prompt collapse (per architect v4), not keep-warm.

risks.title: Schema 1.3 migration must be wrap-style and backwards-compatible with in-flight 1.2 contracts
risks.description: Slice-4 adds Pipeline.no_progress_budget + HITL park decision fields, bumping shared/egg_contracts/models.py schemaVersion 1.2 -> 1.3. Today's migration helpers (_migrate_schema_version_to_1_1 lines 933-962, _migrate_schema_version_to_1_2 lines 964-1014) are run at every Contract.model_validate() (line 948). 1.2 was wrap-style; 1.1 was after-style. A new 1.3 that adds fields with defaults can be after-style — but only if the migration is idempotent AND the defaults are forward-compatible with downstream consumers. There are ~200 existing contracts in .egg-state/contracts/ (the live ones); ANY of them being loaded by upgraded orchestrator code must migrate cleanly. Risk: silent migration corrupts an in-flight contract; or the new fields are populated by old code paths that don't know about them, causing inconsistent state when slice-5's safety-budget consumer reads them.
risks.mitigation: Add to the slice-4 schema-bump task AC: '_migrate_schema_version_to_1_3 is mode=after (the simpler validator path); idempotent; tested against (i) a fresh 1.0 contract, (ii) a fresh 1.1 contract, (iii) a fresh 1.2 contract, (iv) a 1.3 contract loaded twice (no-op).' Add a CI smoke test that loads a representative sample of .egg-state/contracts/* and asserts migration succeeds.

risks.title: Memory file write race between heartbeat thread and event-driven handler
risks.description: Slice-7 adds brc-memory.md write paths from brc_ack/brc_nack handlers. The new wrapper bash also reads this file on every agent boot. If the orchestrator pushes a brc_ack while the wrapper is still writing a memory update from the previous event, the agent could read a partial file. Today's heartbeat thread + state_store path has the same class of risk handled by lockfile semantics.
evidence_files: Architect output runtime_primitive_assumptions.new_primitives_introduced: Per-role memory file `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md` -- in-sandbox-agent filesystem (per-pod, cleaned with pod)
Slice-7 description (action-scaffolded write + atomic tempfile-rename on read)
risks.mitigation: Slice-7 task AC should call out 'atomic tempfile-rename on read' — extend to write path: writers append to a temp file then os.rename (POSIX-atomic). Reader on agent boot opens the canonical path; partial-write window collapses to either old-or-new content. Unit test: write a 10-KB record from two threads concurrently and assert the reader observes the full content of exactly one of the two writes (never a mixed prefix).

risks.title: Per-event Python startup + SDK import cost compounds across many BRC events
risks.description: Each BRC event spawns a fresh python3 -m egg_agent process. Cold Python+SDK import on the orchestrator pod is ~700ms-1.2s today; the egg_agent CLI imports shared/egg_agent/* + the Anthropic/LiteLLM SDK + sandbox/egg_agent_tools schemas. With ~20-40 BRC events per phase, the aggregate startup wall-clock can dominate the cache-read economic win on the cheap (cache-hot) path even if cache-read tokens stay bounded.
evidence_files: shared/egg_agent/__main__.py (egg_agent entry point — measure import cost)
Today's persistent-session wrapper does this once per phase; new wrapper does it per event
risks.mitigation: Slice-1 task-1-2 records per-event wall-clock; task-1-4 report compares aggregate phase wall-clock vs the current persistent-session baseline. If aggregate phase wall-clock regresses by >20%, the spike report surfaces it as a forward-looking note (NOT a stop gate per OSI-2). The cure (if needed) is a warm-Python-runner fallback — out of scope for this issue; tracked as a follow-up note in the spike report.

risks.title: Stateless event-pump must preserve dual-role producer + reviewer ordering (#2749)
risks.description: Today's persistent-session model preserves dual-role producer-FIRST ordering via the agent's own state machine + instruction-text in the BRC preamble. The new event-pump derives next-action from the server (slice-3 consensus next-action endpoint). If the next-action endpoint returns 'REVIEW peer X's proposal' to a dual-role agent that has not yet PROPOSED its own work, the agent self-blocks the BRC round (the exact failure mode #2749 fixed). The server-side derivation must encode producer-FIRST: for dual-role roles, when their own propose_version is 0, the next-action is always 'PROPOSE your work', NOT 'REVIEW peer X'.
evidence_files: Architect d-3 (server-side next-action endpoint, not client-side)
BRC preamble Dual-Role Execution Order banner — producer-first invariant
risks.mitigation: Architect's slice-3 component breakdown must include a dedicated unit test that asserts: given a dual-role agent with propose_version=0, the next-action endpoint returns PROPOSE (not REVIEW) regardless of pending peer proposals. Task_planner must lift this to a slice-3 task AC with explicit test naming.

risks.title: Mass deletion of consensus_wrapper.py code paths breaks dependent tests + ops tooling
risks.description: Slice-6 deletes `MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS` (consensus_wrapper.py line 38), `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (lines 64-99), `_RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT` (lines 102-105), and the `check_confirmed_and_wait` SSE function (lines 397-548). It replaces the SSE consensus.reached blocking path. Today's test surface (tests/orchestrator/test_consensus_wrapper.py) asserts behavior on these symbols. Operational tooling and runbooks reference these names (docs/architecture/orchestrator.md, docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md). Risk: the deletion lands but downstream import sites break the build, OR docs continue to reference deleted concepts and operators reading them are misled. The 3-restart heuristic is also wired into health_monitor.py / startup_reconciliation.py behavior (containers that exit and don't get restarted may now be marked FAILED by reconciliation).
risks.mitigation: Slice-6 deletion ACs must list every downstream reference removed/updated, with grep evidence. Slice-6 tester tasks must remove the now-obsolete restart-path tests in the same commit as the deletion (so the tree isn't briefly red). Slice-6 documenter must sweep docs/architecture/orchestrator.md, docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md, docs/reference/orchestrator-cli.md, sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md for references to the deleted symbols. Add an AC: 'grep -rn for MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS, _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT, _RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT, check_confirmed_and_wait across docs/ and sandbox/agent-config/rules/ returns zero hits.' Also ensure startup_reconciliation.py is updated if the absence of restarts changes how stale containers are detected.

risks.title: CLI prose-arg corruption risk for new egg-orch brc verbs (#2741)
risks.description: Slice-2 adds new CLI verbs (`brc get-state`, `brc list-blocking`, `phase get-context`, `phase get-assigned-tasks`, `consensus resolve-obligation`). Several take prose arguments (`--reason`, `--files-reviewed`, `--note`) that may contain shell metacharacters (`$`, backticks, single/double quotes, newlines). Per #2741, the consensus_wrapper.py has historical regressions where prose substituted into bash templates corrupted the agent's invocation. If new CLI verbs accept prose on argv without shlex.quote (or stdin/file fallback for long prose), the same regression class re-emerges.
evidence_files: Architect d-decisions — new CLI verbs added in slice-2
risks.mitigation: Slice-2 CLI-verb tasks must each have an AC: prose args accept either shlex.quoted argv OR `--<arg>-file PATH` / stdin. A unit test in tests/cli/test_<verb>.py must inject a prose arg containing $, backtick, single-quote, double-quote, newline and assert the server receives it byte-identically. Same rule for the wrapper template's per-event prompt substitution (BC-1 / BC-2 are symmetric exposures).

risks.title: Concurrent slice execution on shared work branch — risk_analyst, architect, task_planner can step on each other

Merge conflicts on .egg-state/agent-outputs/* and .egg-state/contracts/* are mechanically unlikely (different files) but rebase-conflicts are real when the gateway force-syncs. The reviewer also syncs from this branch to review — a producer rebase mid-review window can break the reviewer's git-blame-style citations.

BRC reviewer-sync.md — git fetch origin && git merge origin/<branch> --no-edit

risks.title: Empty acceptance_criteria on the contract — no objective phase-completion target
risks.description: Contract.acceptance_criteria is currently empty (verified via projection). Per the BRC reviewer protocol, plan-phase reviewers (reviewer_plan) gate on slice-level ACs and task-level ACs, but the contract-level acceptance_criteria are the objective phase-completion target. If they're not populated, the plan phase can converge on slice/task ACs without an overall sanity check (e.g. 'the #2906 repro reaches CONFIRMED under the new wrapper'). The prior register's R-12 ACs (1)-(4) need a v2 amend post-TTL-strip: the cache-read AC should be RATIO-based (not TTL-based) and the threshold-language must be instrument-only (OSI-2).

Suggested ACs (v2 post-TTL-strip): (1) the #2906 repro (issue-2270 on qwen3.7-max) reaches CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED on the new wrapper without 'Agent exited without BRC consensus' messages in the run log; (2) per-event cache_read_input_tokens RATIO is reported through the egg-agent harness for both routes on a representative BRC idle (instrument-only — no fail threshold per OSI-2); (3) no MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS / _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT references remain in the codebase post-slice-6; (4) prose args (reason, files_reviewed, note) survive a shell-metachar round-trip uncorrupted on every new CLI verb.

risks.title: Stateless agent loses tool-call context across events — memory file is the only continuity
risks.description: The current persistent-session model keeps the agent's tool-call history (which files were read, which greps were run, partial verdicts in progress) in the conversation context. The event-pump model spawns a fresh agent on each event with only the brc-memory.md snapshot as continuity. If the reviewer started reading a 1000-line file in event N and the agent terminates before reading further, event N+1 doesn't know the read was incomplete. Per OSI-3, brc-memory.md is ephemeral coordination state, not durable session state.
evidence_files: OSI-3 (decision-5 Q2): ephemeral coordination state, NOT durable session state
risks.mitigation: Slice-7 brc-memory.md schema must include: 'in-progress action ledger' — what the agent was doing when the last event closed (e.g. 'reviewing peer architect proposal, read 3/7 files'). The schema is documented in mission.md (slice-8 prompt-collapse output). NACK if slice-7 schema ships without this field.

risks.title: Litellm container log scrape (slice-1 task-1-3) is fragile to log format changes (NARROWED — cost instrumentation only)
risks.description: task-1-3 sources Qwen cache numbers from `kubectl logs deployment/egg-litellm`. The litellm container's structured-log format is owned by upstream litellm (BerriAI) + the custom cost_callback in config/litellm/cost_callback.py. Either changing format breaks the scrape. The cost-callback's stdout format is at config/litellm/cost_callback.py:238-241 (json.dumps). Lower exposure surface, lower likelihood of operator-impacting failure.
evidence_files: Slice-1 task-1-3 — scraping kubectl logs (post-TTL-strip, cost side effect only)

The thin adapter abstraction stays so slice-9 integration tests can use a stdout-tee file in CI (R-2 mitigation symmetry).

risks.title: build_agent_command argv shape — prompt as last positional may need stdin path for very-large prompts
risks.description: shared/egg_agent/command.py:build_agent_command places the user prompt as a single argv positional. POSIX argv length limits (ARG_MAX, typically ~2 MB on Linux) bound the per-event prompt size. With the BRC preamble + tool schemas + mission.md + memory snapshot + event-json, the prompt can grow toward this limit on a long-running pipeline (esp. with verbose NACK reason bodies).
evidence_files: Architect d-decisions — argv-shape of new --memory-file / --event-json flags
risks.mitigation: Slice-5 (event-pump wrapper template) AC: if the assembled per-event prompt exceeds 200 KB, pipe via stdin or a tempfile (--prompt-file PATH) instead of argv. Today's wrapper's shlex.quote substitution into bash template is already a chokepoint that can be extended to detect oversize.

blocking_concerns.title: Shell-prose corruption regression risk (#2741) if event-pump template skips shlex.quote
blocking_concerns.evidence: Today's consensus_wrapper.py:759-762 uses `shlex.quote()` on prompt_text and recovery_user_prompt before substitution into `_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` and ultimately ['bash', '-c', script] at line 775. The new event-pump template (slice-5) regenerates the per-event prompt every iteration from BRC payload (memory snapshot, NACK reasons, files_reviewed lists) — every one of those is prose that can contain $, backticks, quotes, newlines. If task substitutes prompt text into the bash template without shlex.quote (or, equivalently, if it doesn't pipe via stdin / a file), it re-introduces the exact corruption mitigated in #2741. Slice-2's new CLI verbs (`reason` / `files_reviewed` must arrive via stdin or a file path, never argv) are the symmetric exposure (R-8).
blocking_concerns.would_nack_if: slice-5 wrapper-template task does not have an acceptance criterion that says the per-event prompt is passed to python3 -m egg_agent *either* via shlex.quote-applied argv *or* via stdin/file, with a regression-test asserting that a prompt containing shell-metachars round-trips uncorrupted. ALSO NACK if slice-2 CLI-verb tasks accept prose on argv without shlex.quote-aware fallback.
blocking_concerns.mitigation: Add an explicit AC on slice-5 wrapper-template task: the per-event prompt MUST be substituted via shlex.quote (mirroring consensus_wrapper.py:759-760) or piped via a tempfile, AND a unit test in tests/orchestrator/test_consensus_wrapper.py (extended in slice-6 tester task) must inject a prompt containing $, backtick, single-quote, double-quote, newline and assert the agent receives it byte-identically. blocking_concerns.title: Sync-flush durability requires partial-failure semantics, not just success path
blocking_concerns.evidence: Slice-4 adds `_save_pipeline_durable(state)` alongside the existing best-effort `save_pipeline` at orchestrator/state_store.py:672-749. Today's path catches push failure at lines 741-747 and retries on the next save (idempotent best-effort). The new sync-flush path is invoked at exactly the moment the safety-budget consumer needs to know the budget is durably decremented (slice-5 safety-budget consumer task) — if sync-flush silently succeeds-on-local but the remote push fails, a host restart will resurrect the OLD budget and the safety net is undermined. Conversely, if sync-flush raises on push failure, the caller in the event-pump wrapper must NOT crash-loop the agent on transient git/gateway failures (the very class of failure the issue identifies as compounding restart churn). Per cq-3 resolution, the terminal action on budget exhaustion is OVERSEER_ALERT + HITL (NOT auto-FAIL), so the partial-failure path must align with that policy.
blocking_concerns.would_nack_if: slice-4 task ACs do not specify both (a) the success path (returns only after `git push` succeeds) AND (b) the partial-failure path (mock push failure → caller observes the failure AND has a documented bounded retry policy that does NOT restart the agent pod AND aligns with cq-3 OVERSEER_ALERT/HITL terminal action).
blocking_concerns.mitigation: Add to slice-4 AC: 'On push failure, _save_pipeline_durable raises a typed exception (e.g. DurableSaveFailed); the call-site in the safety-budget consumer (slice-5) handles this by emitting an OVERSEER_ALERT and continuing the wait-loop with an in-memory budget snapshot, NOT by exiting the wrapper.' Slice-4 tester task must cover the partial-failure path.
